newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-MARK OF ESTEEM WINS CROWN FOR BRILLIANT DETTORI.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-MARK OF ESTEEM WINS CROWN FOR BRILLIANT DETTORI.

text.p: Mark of Esteem, the 2,000 Guineas winner, proved himself Europe's top miler with a stunning victory in the group one Queen Elizabeth 11 Stakes on Saturday.

Jockey Frankie Dettori, riding his third winner of the day from his first three mounts, took up the running in the final 200 metres to sprint home one and a quarter lengths clear of 1,000 Guineas winner Bosra Sham, trained by Henry Cecil and ridden by Pat Eddery.
Dettori, riding at the peak of his powers, went on to win the subsequent race to make it four out of four.
Although only seven ran in the Queen Elizabeth 11, it was one of the classiest collections of milers seen in Europe for many years.

Dettori said of the 100-30 winner: "I`ve never had that feeling in my life. It was such a quality race yet he was going so easily with a furlong (200 metres) left. He's got to be an exceptional horse. He's undoubtedly the best miler I've riddden."
Third place went to 11-2 chance First Island, the mount of Michael Hills, but French 2,000 Guineas winner Ashkalani, who started 9-4 favourite, finished only fifth.
Mark of Esteem's victory, worth over $310,000, may have effectively clinched the 1996 trainers' championship for Saeed Bin Suroor who handles the Godolphin horses for Sheikh Mohammed of Dubai.

Ironically, it was a dispute last year over Mark of Esteem which led to a split between Cecil and Sheikh Mohammed and ended with the sheikh withdrawing his horses, including Mark of Esteem, from the trainer's Newmarket yard.
Saturday's race was the highlight of the first day of a big two-day festival. Champion Dettori, in brilliant form, won the first two races, also for Bin Suroor and the Godolphin operation.
Bin Suroor is now more than 130,000 pounds ($203,000) clear of Cecil in the trainers' title race.
Sheikh Mohammed said: "If Mark of Esteem is all right he might go for the Breeders' Cup (next month in Toronto)."
Meanwhile, Dettori, riding for a different owner and trainer, won Ascot's fourth race on 7-1 chance Decorated Hero for a 1,351-1 four-timer.
